p-nakedandfamousdenim-5240595579038.d: The MIJ7, Yahan Midnight Selvedge is an unsanforized 17oz slubby Japanese selvedge denim dyed to such a deep shade of indigo that it appears black. Indigo rope dyeing is a delicate process of running cotton yarns through two story dye vats quickly enough that the dye cannot penetrate the core of the yarn. Then the yarn dries and is dipped again, dries and is dipped again. The yarns are dipped dozens of times to achieve that raw denim shade. But here, with just a little black dye added, these yarns have been dyed over and over so many times that they appear black. With wear and age, the opposite process occurs. Each layer of indigo chips away revealing dark blues, then medium bright blues, then light blues, then finally the white core of the yarn. This fabric is made to celebrate the full spectrum of variegated indigo shades. The yarns themselves are irregular, slubby, and woven loosely giving the fabric an organic, uneven grain. The denim is unsanforized but tempi treated, which shrinks the fabric but protects the hairiness, grittiness, and raw denim feel. p-ironheart-10506340630794.d:
Our slim cut jeans, made from 19oz left-hand twill selvedge denim. While most of our denims feature a traditional right-hand twill weave — characterised by a diagonal grain running from the top-right to the bottom-left of the fabric — this “lefty” denim is woven in the opposite direction under very high tension. This creates one of our stiffest, most robust fabrics, with an intense indigo hue that tends to fade with higher contrast than looser weaves.
To create this darkened variation, we take a pair of standard IH-555S-19L jeans and steep the entire garment in black dye using a direct dyeing process. This stains the indigo denim and stitching, with the added bonus of removing all shrinkage from the fabric. A unique middle ground between our traditional indigo and black denims, over time the fabric will gradually fade with blue-tinged hues in high-wear areas.

For years, we had this old 1930s leather fringe jacket hanging in the Wythe office - fun to look at and admire, but that was usually it. The jacket was handmade in the 1930s and was painted a gorgeous yellow color. Over time and wear, the paint had cracked and withered, but the leather was incredibly soft. A long fringe trim hung off the jacket across the front, down the sleeves, and across the back. Panels had been sewn in on each side where a previous owner, maybe the only owner, wanted some extra room to let out the jacket. We loved everything about it.
We were very pleased with our collaborative leather ranch jacket, so we decided to have some fun for ourselves. The Mustang is our nod to the jacket we admired on our wall. We even left in the side panels as a nod to the original owner. This jacket is made from a supple cowhide that needs very little break-in time. Featuring a contrasting collar (on the yellow and green colors), two-way YKK zippers with fringe pullers, smile pockets, fully lined, and just enough fringe to turn heads.

• Fringe trim along the back yoke and down the back of each sleeve
